requests.text:
TWO RENDERER RULES the v3 world needs, both found in the live game today and both fixed in maps2/pipeline/render3.py - please mirror in tiles3.ts.

1. A WALL FACE WHOSE FOOT IS AN INDOOR CELL IS AN INTERIOR FACE. DON'T DRAW IT.
   Maintainer, looking at the smithy from outside: "Why is this door closed?"
   It isn't. The door is a gap in the wall ring, so what shows through the
   opening is the INNER face of the back wall, drawn full height and lit like
   an exterior wall - it reads as a closed plank door. The side walls do the
   same, so the room is boxed in with wall seen from inside.
   Rule: build indoor = every cell under a kind:"roof" or kind:"cave" deck. In
   the wall column, exposed = front_low < zl AND the foot cell (fx,fy) is NOT
   indoor. Everything else is unchanged - the south and east ring faces still
   draw, because their feet stand on grass. Through the doorway you then see
   the floor and the furniture, and it reads as an opening. render3.py:1212.

2. ONE PARQUET FLOOR PER ROOM - the SET, not just the member.
   Maintainer, standing in the town hall: "I said one Parquet Floor per room!!!"
   The floor changes pattern mid-room. Cause: sets are chosen per 24-cell chunk
   and a building straddles chunk borders (the town hall spans x 406-420,
   y 352-363; chunk edges fall at x=408 and y=360), so one room takes two
   different sets.
   Rule: for a cell of indoor floor, choose BOTH the set and the member at the
   ROOM'S ANCHOR - one cell of the connected indoor-floor patch, picked
   deterministically (I use the first in scan order). Same room, same anchor,
   same tile everywhere. render3.py:361-385.

3. THE BLACK CORNER (his indoor screenshot at 411.6,356.1) - I cannot reproduce
   it from the world data and I believe it is yours. I dumped the whole town
   hall: no void cells, every wall cell brown_paving_stone at level 6, every
   floor cell parquet_floor at level 0, one roof deck at level 6 thickness 0
   over the whole 15x12 footprint. Nothing black is authored anywhere in it -
   roofs stopped being black_rock in 5cdded6c64, and the wall tops render grey
   in his own screenshot. What the shot shows is wall stubs where some have
   their top face drawn (grey) and one does not (dark and untopped), with black
   beside it. That looks like the indoor cut (indoorTop = roomFloor + dial)
   truncating a column without re-capping it. The internal wall lines are at
   x=413 and y=358, and the corner where they meet is (413,358).
